Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with a wrist fracture
consistent in kind and mechanism with the force of the impact. Over the course of 30
office visits, care proceeded along a typical trajectory: immobilization, serial
radiographic follow-up, supervised progressive range-of-motion work, and graduated
strengthening. Visit frequency decreased steadily as function returned and pain
diminished. On examination, lcoalized tenderness and reduced grip strength over the
affected wrist correlate with the documented fracture, while several neurovascular and
stability tests returned within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury to
this area, and no earlier treatment records for the wrist were identified. Billing for
the episode reflects single, non-duplicated charges for each service rendered. At last
review, the patient had regained most functional motion and was discharged to home
exercise with instructions to return if symptoms recur.
</page>
